--- title: "Indicators, dissemination and the way forward" subtitle: "Turning the accounts into information, and producing them every year" author: - name: Renato Vargas - name: Achille Pegoue lang: en-US bibliography: ../../../assets/references.bib csl: ../../../assets/apa-en.csl execute: echo: false warning: false format: revealjs: theme: [simple, ../../../assets/slides.scss] footer: "Energy and emissions accounts for Tunisia" slide-number: true width: 1100 height: 700 title-slide-attributes: class: theme-title data-state: sans-pied --- ## What this presentation covers {.theme-content} 1. Who uses energy and emissions accounts, and for what. 2. Core indicators and dissemination formats. 3. What it takes to produce the accounts every year. # Indicators and dissemination ## Who uses the accounts - **Energy and climate policy**: which industries drive demand and emissions, and where efficiency gains matter. - **Economic planning**: the energy and emission content of growth. - **Modelling**: input-output and general equilibrium models need energy and emissions by industry. - **International reporting**: SEEA, Eurostat and OECD formats, and comparison with other countries. ## Core indicators | Indicator | Accounts | Unit | |:--|:--|:--| | Net domestic energy use | PEFA | PJ | | Energy intensity of value added | PEFA + SUT | TJ per million TND | | Household energy use per unit of spending | PEFA + SUT | TJ per million TND | | Emissions by industry and gas | AEA | kt CO2 eq | | Emission intensity of value added | AEA + SUT | t CO2 eq per million TND | | Household emissions per unit of spending | AEA + SUT | t CO2 eq per million TND | ## Energy and emissions move together ::: {#1957fa6a .cell fig-height='4.4' fig-width='10' execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/cell-4-output-1.png){width=1480 height=649} ::: ::: ## Reading the chart - Industries that use more energy per dinar also emit more per dinar. - Industries above the general pattern emit for reasons other than fuel: cement (process CO2), agriculture (methane), waste (landfills). - Both scales are logarithmic: the range between industries is very wide. ## The place of households - Households used 34% of energy end use in 2022 (34% in 2015). - They emitted 11% of greenhouse gases in 2022 (10% in 2015). - Their emissions come from cars and homes; firewood, a large part of their energy, counts as biomass outside the CO2 total. ## Dissemination formats - **Tables**: supply and use tables, accounts by activity and gas, bridge tables, indicators. - **Workbooks** in three languages, produced by the same code. - **Documents** whose text reads the data, and **interactive charts** on the web. - **Open data**: stable codes and separate label tables. ## A dissemination calendar - Accounts for year *t* as soon as the balance, the inventory and the supply and use tables for *t* are available. - Revisions follow those of the sources; the pipeline recompiles the whole series in a minute. - Metadata and revision notes accompany each release. # The way forward ## What exists now {.theme-content} - A complete first compilation of both accounts, 2015 to 2022. - An open pipeline that reproduces the IMF tools and runs in under a minute. - Documents, Excel products in three languages and a data explorer. - A list of assumptions and open questions, each recorded in a lookup table. ## An annual cycle ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A["New balance (ONEM),
inventory (ANME),
SUT (INS)"] --> B["Add files to
data/sources/"] B --> C["Run the pipeline
and its checks"] C --> D["Review lookups
with data producers"] D --> C C --> E["Publish workbooks,
documents, explorer"] ``` ## Roles | Task | Who | |:--|:--| | Provide the energy balance, in a stable layout | ONEM | | Provide the CRT workbooks | ANME and inventory partners | | Provide the supply and use tables | INS, national accounts | | Run the pipeline, review lookups, publish | INS, environmental accounts | | Validate allocation choices | INS with ONEM and ANME | ## Priorities for the coming year 1. Validate the allocation assumptions with ONEM, ANME and the national accounts. 2. Obtain residence data for international transport. 3. Train a team at the INS to run and maintain the pipeline. 4. Agree on a first publication and its calendar. 5. Extend to air pollutants and energy asset accounts when data allow. ## Skills and tools - Python with `uv`: one command to install, one to compile. - Lookup tables in CSV: edited in Excel, reviewed on GitHub. - Quarto for documents and the website. - The IMF tools remain the reference for checking. ## Points to discuss - Which indicators belong in INS publications, and which in a dedicated release? - Who leads the accounts at the INS, and with which team? - Formal agreements on data transmission with ONEM and ANME? - Hosting of the code and the website? ## References ::: {#refs} :::
